h1: DoD Cyber Awareness Challenge Practice Quiz & Test Questions
subhead: Take a free practice quiz or snap a photo of any Cyber Awareness Challenge question for an instant, explained answer — finish your annual training without getting stuck.
metaTitle: DoD Cyber Awareness Challenge Quiz & Practice Test | Cambo
metaDescription: Free DoD Cyber Awareness Challenge quiz and practice test questions with instant, explained answers. Point your phone at any training question and get unstuck in seconds.
whyItWorks: The Cyber Awareness Challenge covers a lot of ground fast — phishing, PII handling, spillage, insider threat, removable media — and it's easy to blank on a specific rule mid-question. Cambo reads the exact question on your screen and gives you the right answer plus the reasoning, so you finish the module instead of rereading the same slide twice.

sampleQuestions.q: Which of the following is a best practice for protecting Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI)?
options: Email it to your personal account so you can work on it from home
Save it to any removable media so that a backup always exists
Store it only on authorized systems and encrypt it both at rest and in transit
Post it to a shared team folder with open permissions for convenience
sampleQuestions.a: Store CUI only on authorized systems and encrypt it both at rest and in transit — never email it to a personal account or save it to removable media that isn't approved.

sampleQuestions.q: You receive an email from an unfamiliar sender asking you to verify your CAC PIN by clicking a link. What should you do?
options: Click the link but enter only the first two digits of your PIN
Reply to the sender and ask them to confirm their identity first
Forward it to your team so they know to expect the same request
Don't click the link — report it as suspected phishing, since DoD systems never ask for your PIN through an email link
sampleQuestions.a: Don't click the link. Report it as suspected phishing — legitimate DoD systems never ask you to enter your PIN through an email link.

sampleQuestions.q: You suspect classified information may have been introduced onto an unclassified system (a "spillage"). What should you do first?
options: Immediately report it to your security manager or the appropriate incident response channel
Delete the files right away to contain the exposure
Keep working normally and raise it at the next staff meeting
Copy the files to removable media so they can be reviewed later
sampleQuestions.a: Immediately report it to your security manager or the appropriate incident response channel. Don't try to delete the files or keep working on the system — that can destroy evidence needed to contain the spillage.

sampleQuestions.q: You find a USB drive in the parking lot labeled "Salary Info FY26." What should you do?
options: Plug it into an isolated personal laptop to identify the owner
Leave it where you found it in case the owner comes back
Turn it in to your security office without plugging it into any device
Plug it into a government workstation so antivirus can scan it
sampleQuestions.a: Don't plug it into any government or personal device. Turn it in to your security office — unknown removable media is a classic malware vector, and curiosity-driven plugging-in is exactly what this scenario tests.

sampleQuestions.q: Which of the following is a potential insider threat indicator?
options: An employee who occasionally takes leave on short notice
An employee who prefers to work from a quiet part of the office
An employee who frequently asks questions about other teams' projects
Unexplained affluence combined with unusual work hours or attempts to access information outside their need-to-know
sampleQuestions.a: Unexplained affluence combined with unusual work hours or attempts to access information outside their need-to-know — behavioral and financial red flags, not just technical ones, are what the training emphasizes.

sampleQuestions.q: Which social media practice creates the greatest security risk?
options: Posting details about upcoming deployments, unit movements, or specific mission information
Following official DoD accounts from a personal profile
Using a profile photo that was taken while in uniform
Connecting with former colleagues from a previous duty station
sampleQuestions.a: Posting details about upcoming deployments, unit movements, or specific mission information. Even seemingly harmless posts can aggregate into an OPSEC risk when combined with other public information.

sampleQuestions.q: A person you don't recognize asks you to hold the secure door open because their badge isn't working. What should you do?
options: Hold the door — badge readers malfunction frequently
Hold the door if the person is wearing a visible ID badge
Politely decline and direct them to the visitor center or security desk to be verified
Let them in and report it to security afterward
sampleQuestions.a: Politely decline and direct them to the visitor center or security desk to be verified — this is "tailgating," and holding the door bypasses the access control the badge system exists to enforce.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the best way to protect against malicious code?
options: Disable antivirus scanning so it doesn't interfere with system updates
Keep antivirus software and system patches up to date, and avoid links or attachments from unverified senders
Only open attachments that are in PDF format
Rely on the network firewall, which blocks all malicious code
sampleQuestions.a: Keep antivirus software and system patches up to date, and avoid clicking links or opening attachments from unverified senders — most malicious code enters through phishing or unpatched vulnerabilities.

faqs.q: How long does the DoD Cyber Awareness Challenge take?
faqs.a: Most people finish in 60-90 minutes, depending on how many modules your service branch requires and how quickly you move through the knowledge checks.

faqs.q: Do I have to retake it every year?
faqs.a: Yes — it's an annual requirement for anyone with access to DoD networks or systems, including contractors and service members.

faqs.q: Can I use Cambo during the actual training?
faqs.a: Yes. Cambo works on any question you can photograph, including the ones inside the official training portal — point your camera at the question and get an explained answer in seconds.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with the DoD or the official Cyber Awareness Challenge?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool. It's not produced, endorsed, or affiliated with the Department of Defense.

faqs.q: What topics does the Cyber Awareness Challenge cover?
faqs.a: Phishing and social engineering, handling of PII/PHI and CUI, spillage, malicious code, removable media, social networking risks, insider threat indicators, and physical and facility security.

faqs.q: What happens if I fail a knowledge check?
faqs.a: Most versions let you review the material and retake the check — there's usually no limit on attempts, just a requirement to pass before you get your completion certificate.
